name: Queen's Gambit Declined
goal: As Black against the Queen's Gambit, you can hold the centre with e6, develop, castle, and know which pieces still need to come out.
intro: In the Queen's Gambit Declined, Black answers 2.c4 with 2...e6. The e-pawn backs up the pawn on d5, so Black keeps a pawn in the centre and the bishop on f8 can come out. The cost is the other bishop: the pawn on e6 shuts in the bishop on c8. You develop the kingside, castle, and then look for a way to free that bishop.

parts.title: Hold d5, develop, castle
parts.keyIdea: Hold d5 with pawns, develop the kingside and castle; the bishop on c8 is the piece that still needs a plan.
parts.text: You are Black, and White opens with 1.d4. The line is the Orthodox Defence as Lichess's list of openings names it. At each move, ask what it does for your centre, your pieces and your king.
parts.line: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 Nbd7

notes.text: 1...d5 meets White's centre pawn with one of your own. It also makes e4 hard for White to play, because your pawn on d5 attacks that square.

2.c4 attacks your d5 pawn. 2...e6 guards it with a pawn, so if White takes on d5 you take back with the e-pawn and still have a pawn in the centre. It also opens a path for the bishop on f8, but the bishop on c8 is now shut in behind e6.
3.Nc3 adds a second attacker on d5. 3...Nf6 brings out a knight that guards d5 once more and stops White from playing e4.
4.Bg5 pins your knight: if the knight moved away, the bishop could take your queen. 4...Be7 steps in between, so the pin is gone, and it gets your king one step closer to castling.
5.e3 opens the way for White's other bishop. Castle now with 5...O-O, so your king is safe before the centre opens. 5...h6, asking the bishop on g5 to decide, is just as good.

6...Nbd7 develops your last knight. It goes to d7, not c6, so your c-pawn stays free to move to c6 or c5. Of your minor pieces, only the bishop on c8 is still at home: one plan is ...c6, ...dxc4 and ...Nd5 to trade some pieces, then ...e5 to open its diagonal; another is ...b6 and ...Bb7.
